::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[How do we say in English that pyramid is not skewed?](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1135531/how-do-we-say-in-english-that-pyramid-is-not-skewed), asked by [studying](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/213349/studying) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2015-02-05; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I would like to know if there is a term kind of "straight pyramid"? I mean, is there a word for a pyramid such that the line segment from the apex to the center of the base is perpendicular to the base.
:::

I believe the term you are looking for is *right*.

From [mathwords.com](http://www.mathwords.com/r/right_pyramid.htm):

> **right pyramid**: A pyramid that has its apex aligned directly above the center of the base.
